Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: orthographic albedo texture-source painting for an existing 3D model.
Input 1 is the sole EDIT TARGET and strict geometry authority: the plain grey orthographic guide. Input 2 is design_reference.png, the approved three-quarter HD design, sole colour/material/design reference. Input 3 is concept_crop.png, supporting original concept reference.
Paint ONLY the existing surfaces of input 1, precisely registered onto its 1024 x 1024 canvas. Keep every original silhouette pixel, size, position, shape edge, facet, opening, overlap, rubble block and small base fragment identical. Preserve the exact orthographic camera and the broken headless neck. Do not rotate toward the reference's three-quarter view, redesign, add or remove geometry, recenter, rescale or crop. No extra rubble or details outside the guide silhouette.
Materials: white-and-bone ceramic stone, weathered and chipped, subtle hairline cracks and brownish chipped erosion like the approved design; thin tarnished gold trim on robe hem and sash and belt; grey-violet ash as pigment in folds and on the plinth. Match the approved design's material colours, but NOT its lighting. Paint consistent materials onto the exact guide geometry.
LIGHTING: pure albedo, even flat shadowless illumination from the viewer. No cast shadows, no ambient-occlusion darkening, no directional light or gradient shading, no strong specular highlights or reflections, no rim light. Folds and recesses stay legible through material colour and fine texture, not baked dark shadows. Any glowing parts are painted at their glowing colour without casting light; do not invent glowing parts.
Output: exactly one 1024 x 1024 PNG with actual transparent background, preserving the guide transparency and antialiased edges. No background, floor, drop shadow, text, labels, layout or multiple views. The result is a direct surface repaint of the guide with unchanged outline and internal shape boundaries.
View: LEFT, exactly as guide_left.png: the long surviving arm is visible on the left side of the body, the chest faces image-right, the large diagonal foreground slab descends toward image-right. Preserve this view exactly.
